scope: Linux x64 private file-worker allocation repair. Bounded short-read comparisons, packaged mains and targeted unchanged upstream tests; not complete filesystem or memory-capacity parity.
findings: Before the repair, a three-byte read and a zero-byte EOF result each carried a backing allocation equal to the requested 1, 16, or 64 MiB in Node, Deno and released Bun. The response cloner copied unused capacity.

The worker now copies only returned bytes from partial or pooled views into a fresh Uint8Array, then transfers it. Full independent allocations retain their direct transfer path. Observed backing sizes are now 3 and 0 bytes in every engine.

The identical ordinary Lean short-read, EOF and zero-length-read fixture passes all twelve native/full-engine controls both before and after. Released-engine packaged mains pass nine further controls.

Four maintained host tests cover short and full reads, EOF, pooled line results, retained earlier results, and errors followed by successful operations. Eighteen unchanged upstream IO, filesystem and HTTP registrations pass with all 7267 original hashes intact.
measurementLimits: Each memory peak is one isolated guarded run, not a statistical benchmark. Requests never exceed 64 MiB. The native fread allocation still reserves the requested capacity; this repair removes copies and retained capacity at worker response boundaries.
retainedDevelopmentAttempts: The first package probe placed its source beside unrelated permission-denied experiment directories. Project fingerprinting failed before compilation. The retry builds a byte-identical source in an isolated fixture directory; the failed attempt remains retained.
remainingGaps: Native Windows, macOS and ARM64 validation remains unexecuted.
Full Bun compiler comparisons use the disclosed local memory64-capacity build and Linux stack helper; direct host and packaged checks use released Bun.
Multi-GiB IO equivalence, complete upstream suites and packaged full-runtime integration remain unfinished. No remaining difference is established fundamental.
